ground_truth: close() is the only method touching self._conn without holding self._lock, so teardown can free the SQLite connection while a background daemon thread is mid-execute, giving a use-after-free in the sqlite3 C extension.

graded_by.who: objective culprit match against fix commit bda0802, format-tolerant parse

notes: FULLY SELF-CONTAINED PIPELINE. Stage 0: each of 4 models asked what convention the class follows and how to audit it -- prompt never mentions lock, close, or bugs, and forbids diagnosing. All 8/8 samples derived the lock-discipline invariant unaided. Rule taken verbatim from mistral-small: 'Ensure every method contains a with self._lock: block around any database operations involving _conn.' Stage 1: 16 candidates generated; close present 3/16; majority vote returns mark_result_published (WRONG). Stage 2: the same 4 models verify the deduplicated candidate list (counts stripped) against the MODEL-DERIVED rule. Result: close, 3/4. Identical to the run using an experimenter-written rule, so supplying the rule bought nothing. No model above 14.3GB and no frontier model in the loop. gemma2:2b (1.6GB) dissented in both runs -- it hallucinated that close() does not touch self._conn -- placing the comprehension floor between 1.6 and 7.2GB. gemma4:latest reached close by reasoning but emitted 'Candidate:' instead of 'CULPRIT:' and was truncated; scored by a format-tolerant parser. KEY MECHANISM: gemma4:e2b generated mark_result_published 17/17 across all runs and never once produced close, yet verified close correctly -- a within-model generate/verify asymmetry. The population's role is coverage, not insight.
